subject: Discovery recap: EmedCo proprietary API offramp (first meeting)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@emedco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: EmedCo proprietary API offramp (first meeting)

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and agreed, plus immediate next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Vendor lock: heavy dependence on OpenAI + Anthropic for generation and embeddings; difficult to control costs or tune behavior.
- Cost volatility: token spend spikes during campaign bursts and chat usage.
- Latency & throttling: occasional p95 spikes impacting real-time UIs.
- Data residency / PHI: some classification & routing must remain inside a controlled environment for a subset of users.

Current stack you described:
- Gen API: OpenAI (gpt-4o family) for chat/generation, Anthropic for a small number of high-assurance flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for search & ranking (~600M tokens/mo equivalent).
- Orchestration: in-house gateway (Kong) + cloud functions; some L2 caching at edge.

Success criteria you called out:
- Functional parity on top-2 user journeys (support chat & snippet generation) with no more than 2% increase in hallucination/QA failures measured by your existing test suite.
- Latency p95 <= 350ms for typical 1.5k token contexts.
- Cost target: reduce per-token unit cost by >=30% in steady state, with clear burst model.
- Integration: SDK parity for function-calling/webhook flows; transparent traceability for auditing.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; HIPAA desirable for PHI workflows — private deployment option preferred for those flows.

What we’ll deliver next (by EOD Thu):
- Shortlist of 3 open-model candidate configurations mapped to your success criteria + rough TCO (attached).
- Migration checklist tailored to EmedCo (SteppingStone-Migration-Checklist.xlsx).
- Proposed agenda for a technical deep-dive (60 min) with your infra and security teams.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Send the current infra/architecture diagram and where PHI is stored (attachment would be fine).
- Share any internal eval prompts or unit tests you use for hallucination checks so we can bench the candidate models against them.

I’ve attached an initial fit brief (redwood-open-model-fit.pdf) and a migration checklist. Proposed times for the deep-dive next week: Wed 10/27 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 10/28 14:00–15:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced: SteppingStone-Migration-Checklist.xlsx, redwood-open-model-fit.pdf
From: Alyssa Cho <alyssa.cho@emedco.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@emedco.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: EmedCo proprietary API offramp (first meeting)

Thanks Stephanie — this looks right and is very helpful. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

Clarifications:
- Core generation traffic is ~120K requests/day, average 800 tokens/request; embeddings are about 600M tokens/month as you noted.
- Models currently in production: OpenAI gpt-4o (generation), Anthropic Claude-2 for safety-sensitive flows. We also run a small on-prem ranker for PII filtering.
- PHI: customer support transcripts contain PHI for ~8% of sessions; those must remain in a controlled environment per our contract.

Priorities & constraints:
- Procurement timeline: renewal discussion Q1 2027 — any platform migration would need a solid POC by end of Nov to be considered for compliance reviews for procurement.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required; FedRAMP not required yet but worth calling out.

I attached a simplified infra diagram (EmedCo-infra-diagram.png) and a short list of our internal hallucination tests (will share in a follow-up email).

Deep-dive: Wed 10/27 10:00 PT works for me. Invite our Security lead (sarah.lee@emedco.com) and Eng manager (mike.gonzalez@emedco.com).

Thanks,
Alyssa
Head of Platform Engineering — EmedCo
alyssa.cho@emedco.com

Attachment referenced: EmedCo-infra-diagram.png
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: EmedCo proprietary API offramp (first meeting)

Internal — quick notes from my side after reading the infra diagram and Alyssa’s constraints:
- Candidate model configs to propose for POC (mapping to their success criteria):
  1) Redwood-Mistral-30B-tuned (int8/qat) — good latency/cost balance for chat flows, proven in our latency SLOs.
  2) Redwood-Llama-70B-compat-q4_k — stronger long-context behavior, better for document synthesis use cases (slightly higher cost).
  3) Hybrid: Redwood-Tiny-embed + Redwood-Llama-70B for generation (offload embeddings to a smaller quantized instance to hit cost targets).
- For PHI paths, recommend a Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logging; include a plan for redaction/PII filters in the early router.
- Need Alyssa’s hallucination test suite and a sample of real transcripts (sanitized) to run our regression checks.

I’ll draft the POC scope and the TCO spreadsheet today and attach to Stephanie’s email before EOD.

— Ben
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
